headline: A conditional optimization method allocates inference budgets across complementary language models
summary: An October 29 arXiv paper studies allocating repeated-sampling inference budgets across language models. It proves the general allocation problem NP-hard and gives an efficient global optimization method under a stated diminishing-returns condition: each model’s per-query log-failure reduction must be nondecreasing and concave in spend. On four coding and agentic benchmarks, the authors report a better solve-rate/cost frontier than any single model, with larger gains where model strengths complement one another; a greedy sequential order is within 10% of the best fixed order at median, while cheapest-first can spend up to 16% more. The results use recorded trials, sometimes only four or five per model/query, and a mix of observed prices, public price snapshots and compute proxies. They are paper-reported, not an independent reproduction or evidence of real marketplace revenue and price effects.
